note.explanation: Plants need mineral nutrients from the soil to make important substances and grow. Macronutrients are needed in large quantities, while micronutrients are needed in small quantities. Nitrogen is used to make proteins and chlorophyll; magnesium is part of chlorophyll.
examples: Potassium is a macronutrient because plants need it in larger quantities.
Iron is a micronutrient because plants need it in lower quantities.
note.checkAnswer: Nitrogen is needed for proteins and chlorophyll; magnesium is a component of chlorophyll and activates many enzymes.
note.simple: Plants take useful minerals from the soil. They need some minerals a lot and others only a little.

mcqs.stem: Which role of nitrogen is stated in your textbook?
rationales: Nitrogen is a component of proteins and chlorophyll.
Potassium, not nitrogen, regulates the opening and closing of the stoma.
Molybdenum is a component of the enzyme that converts nitrates to ammonia.

mcqs.stem: Which mineral is a component of chlorophyll and activates many enzymes?
rationales: Iron is necessary for photosynthesis and activates many enzymes, but it is not identified as a chlorophyll component here.
Magnesium is a component of chlorophyll and activates many enzymes.
Calcium activates enzymes and is a structural component of cell walls, but is not listed as a chlorophyll component.
Sulphur is a component of proteins, vitamins and enzymes, but is not listed as a chlorophyll component.

mcqs.stem: In what form do plant roots absorb nitrogen, according to the section?
rationales: The section states that plant roots absorb nitrogen in the form of nitrates.
The section does not state that nitrogen is absorbed as phosphate ions.
The section does not state that nitrogen is absorbed as sulphate ions.
The section does not state that nitrogen is absorbed as chloride ions.

mcqs.stem: What is the yellowing of leaves caused by insufficient chlorophyll called?
rationales: The section names yellowing caused by insufficient chlorophyll chlorosis.
Guttation is not the term used for yellowing of leaves in this section.
Transpiration is not the term used for yellowing of leaves in this section.
Germination is the beginning of growth from a seed, not yellowing of leaves.

mcqs.stem: Which deficiencies can cause yellowing to appear first in older leaves?
rationales: Nitrogen deficiency can cause this pattern, but it is not the only one.
Magnesium deficiency can cause this pattern, but it is not the only one.
For either deficiency, the plant moves the element from older to younger leaves, so yellowing is first seen in old leaves.
Both deficiencies can cause yellowing to appear first in older leaves.

explain.title: Nutrition and nutrients
explain.body: Nutrition means the processes in which food is prepared or obtained and converted into body substances for growth and energy. Nutrients are the substances required by organism for energy, growth, repair, and maintenance.

explain.title: Mineral nutrients
explain.body: Mineral nutrients are special chemical elements absorbed from soil that are essential for plants to grow. Plants need these materials, in addition to the materials used in photosynthesis, to make other biomolecules.

explain.title: Two groups of minerals
explain.body: The minerals which are required in larger quantities are called macronutrients, for example carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, potassium, nitrogen, sulphur, calcium, and magnesium. The minerals which are required in lower quantities are called micronutrients, for example iron, molybdenum, boron, copper, manganese, zinc, chlorine, and nickel.

explain.title: Nitrogen and magnesium
explain.body: Nitrogen is a necessary part of proteins, enzymes, nucleic acids and chlorophyll. Roots absorb nitrogen in the form of nitrates. Magnesium is part of chlorophyll and activates many plant enzymes; roots absorb it in ionic form (Mg²⁺).

explain.title: Chlorosis
explain.body: A shortage of nitrogen or magnesium can cause chlorophyll to become insufficient and leaves to turn yellow. This yellowing is called chlorosis. The plant moves nitrogen or magnesium from older to younger leaves, so yellowing is seen in old leaves first.

mistakes: Do not swap the definitions: macronutrients are needed in larger quantities; micronutrients are needed in lower quantities.
Do not say that nitrogen is absorbed as magnesium ions; the section says roots absorb nitrogen as nitrates and magnesium as Mg²⁺.
Do not describe magnesium as only an enzyme activator; it is also a component of chlorophyll.
Use chlorosis for yellowing due to insufficient chlorophyll, not as the name for a mineral nutrient.
